course_name_en: Refrigeration, Air Conditioning and Heat Pump Technology 2
prerequisites: Basic knowledge from Thermodynamics and Fluid Mechanics provided by MABB310 and MABB410, especially: understanding of fundamental thermodynamic and fluid mechanical principles and laws, basics of heat transfer.

learning_outcomes.text: After completing the module, students are able to thoroughly evaluate the energetic and ecological significance of air conditioning systems and heat pumps with concrete reference to their use in buildings, and to apply meteorological and thermo-physiological principles to the planning and analysis of building energy technology systems.
They can name influencing factors of thermal comfort, evaluate them using PMV and PPD indicators, and computationally capture central air treatment processes and represent them in suitable diagrams.
Furthermore, they are capable of calculating cooling loads, heating loads, and air volume flows for the design of building technical systems.
In this context, students design, calculate, and analyze processes and systems.
They independently solve specific problems and critically question the application and significance of the technologies.

syllabus_topics: The basic structure of building energy technology systems is taught. The focus is on heat supply using renewable energies, especially through heat pumps.
Classification of buildings by typology (residential buildings, non-residential buildings, special buildings).
Structure of building energy technology based on the three-part division of supply concepts according to generation, distribution, and delivery; central and decentralized systems.
Single building supply vs. district heating supply.
Renewable and conventional heat generators, especially heat pumps.
Heat distribution (hydraulic networks and distribution systems, hydraulic circuits and basic fittings).
Design of main components (heat generators, storage systems).
Evaluation and classification of the quality of energy supply concepts (system efficiency factors, CO2 emissions, COP, JAZ, SCOP, eta-S), legal requirements.
Introduction to ventilation and air conditioning technology and knowledge of the most important components and systems of room air technology and air conditioning systems.
Meteorological basics: atmosphere, solar radiation, air humidity, air temperature, wind.
Physiological and technological requirements for air conditioning technology: thermal comfort, cooling load, heating demand.

Thermodynamics of air treatment: characteristic values and state changes of moist air, Mollier h,X diagram: heating, cooling and dehumidification, humidification with liquid water and steam, pressure increase with fans, humidification and dehumidification with sorption.
Design of air conditioning systems: cooling load calculation, heating load calculation, outside air volume flow, supply air volume flow.
Air conditioning units and central systems: structure of air conditioning units and central systems, fans, heat exchangers, humidifiers and dehumidifiers, air filters, air ducts.
Air flows in air-conditioned rooms: chilled ceilings; basics, forms and types of air outlets, application examples (e.g., residential ventilation).
Measurement and control in air conditioning technology: measurement of air velocities, temperatures, air humidity, air volume flows; control of air conditioning systems and their components.
Heat recovery in air conditioning technology: regenerators, recuperators.
assessment_rules: The module is assessed by two written exams, each lasting 60 minutes. The exam in MABB641D accounts for 50% of the final grade, and the exam in MABB642D accounts for the remaining 50%. Additionally, coursework consisting of lab reports in MABB642D is required.
